name: Ashwagandha
short: Case reports link ashwagandha to liver injury (jaundice, itching), with deaths in people who already had cirrhosis, and to thyrotoxicosis in one reported case.
text: A scoping review of 13 publications (25 patients) of case reports and case series described liver injury attributed to ashwagandha that typically developed after weeks of use, most often with a cholestatic or mixed pattern presenting with jaundice and itching; most patients recovered over weeks to months after stopping, but there was one case of acute liver failure requiring transplantation and three deaths among patients with pre-existing cirrhosis. The authors of that review concluded that people with advanced chronic liver disease should be counselled to avoid ashwagandha, and a case series from India likewise reported acute-on-chronic liver failure with high mortality in those with pre-existing liver disease. A single case report describes thyrotoxicosis with a fast heart rhythm (supraventricular tachycardia) in a 73-year-old woman after two years of taking ashwagandha root extract, which resolved after she stopped it. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
